question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
gold_answer: Pre-existing diseases are excluded until 48 months of continuous coverage has elapsed from first inception (clause 4.1). Definition 3.26: any condition with signs, symptoms, diagnosis or treatment within 48 months before the first policy.

question: Diabetes ke liye waiting period kitna hai?
gold_answer: Diabetes and related complications have a 2 year specific waiting period (4.3 ii n). If diabetes already exists at first policy, 4.1 applies: excluded until 48 months of continuous coverage, including complications such as retinopathy, nephropathy, foot or wound, angiopathy, neuropathy, hyper or hypoglycaemic shock, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular accident.
notes: PRE-FILLED, needs human check. VERIFY: the text does not say explicitly which period prevails for diabetes existing at inception. A good answer states both.

question: Is there a specific waiting period for cataract, knee replacement or hernia?
key_phrases: Two years waiting period|joint replacement due to degenerative conditions
gold_answer: Cataract and hernia: 2 years. Joint replacement due to degenerative conditions: 4 years (age related osteoarthritis and osteoporosis also 4 years). Clause 4.3. Knee replacement maps to joint replacement due to degenerative conditions.

question: Is the initial 30 day waiting period applicable to accidents?
key_phrases: This shall not apply in case the insured person is hospitalised for injuries
gold_answer: The first 30 day exclusion (4.2) does not apply to hospitalisation for injuries from an accident that occurred after inception of the first policy. Illnesses contracted in the first 30 days are excluded.

question: What is the room rent limit?
key_phrases: 1% of sum insured per day subject to maximum
gold_answer: Room, boarding and nursing: 1% of sum insured per day, maximum Rs 5,000. ICU: 2% of sum insured per day, maximum Rs 10,000. Total under section 2.1 capped at 25% of sum insured for any one illness. Sub-limits do not apply for hospitalisation in a PPN or for Ayurveda and Homeopathy.

gold_answer: ICU has its own separate limit: 2% of sum insured per day, maximum Rs 10,000, instead of the 1% per day, Rs 5,000 limit for a normal room (clause 2.1).

question: Is maternity covered, and after how long?
gold_answer: Not covered. Clause 4.7 excludes treatment arising from pregnancy or childbirth including caesarean section, miscarriage, abortion and complications, other than ectopic pregnancy established by medical reports. The policy offers no maternity cover after any waiting period.

question: Are AYUSH treatments covered?
key_phrases: admissible up to 20% of the sum insured
gold_answer: Ayurveda and Homeopathy are covered up to 20% of sum insured for any one illness, and the section 2.1 to 2.3 sub-limits do not apply to them. Unani and Siddha appear in the definition 3.2 but clause 4.15 excludes alternative treatments other than Ayurveda and Homeopathy. The document does not use the term AYUSH.

question: Are daycare procedures covered?
key_phrases: Day care procedures will include following day care surgeries
gold_answer: Yes. Day care treatment (3.9) means treatment under general or local anaesthesia in under 24 hours that would otherwise need 24 hours of hospitalisation. Appendix I lists 140 procedures. Other procedures needing under 24 hours require prior approval from company or TPA. Standard exclusions and waiting periods still apply.

question: Is treatment for mental illness covered?
gold_answer: Not covered. Clause 4.10 excludes all psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders, intentional self inflicted injury and attempted suicide.

question: Kya cashless treatment kisi bhi hospital mein mil jata hai?
key_phrases: is subject to pre authorization by the TPA
gold_answer: No. Cashless is available only at network providers or PPN, with pre authorization by the TPA (5.5.2). Inform TPA at least 72 hours before planned admission, or within 24 hours of emergency admission (5.5.1). If cashless is denied, treat and claim reimbursement. The hospital list is not in the document.

question: How many days of pre and post hospitalisation expenses are covered?
key_phrases: 30 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalised|60 days immediately after
gold_answer: Pre hospitalisation: 30 days before admission. Post hospitalisation: 60 days after discharge. Both for the same condition and only if the hospitalisation claim is admissible. Clauses 3.24 and 3.25.

question: Is there a no claim bonus, and what happens to it after a claim?
key_phrases: increased by 5% in respect of each claim free policy period
gold_answer: Yes, cumulative bonus (2.4.1): sum insured excluding CB rises 5% for each claim free policy period with continuous renewal, up to 50%. After a claim, the CB percentage is reduced by 5% of sum insured at the next renewal; the base sum insured is not reduced.
